Tractate on Education

Ornate rhetorick taught out of the rule of Plato…. To which poetry would be made subsequent, or indeed rather precedent, as being less suttle and fine, but more simple, sensuous, and passionate.

—
Tractate on Education

John

Milton

Harvard Classics, Vol. 3, Part 4

Tractate on Education From the Edition of 1673

John Milton

In the vein of Plato’s 
Republic
 before it and Rousseau’s 
Emile
 after, 
On Education
 is a personal epistle aimed at the training of youth in the classic and poetic traditions as well as the future of scientific studies.
